newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Hi-Bred says corn Bt gene okayed.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Hi-Bred says corn Bt gene okayed.

text.p: Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc said Monday it was notified that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has approved Monsanto Co's Bt gene, which Pioneer licenses to protect its corn hybrids from the European corn borer.
Pioneer said these genetically alterred corn hybrids containing the Bt gene will be available for planting in 1997.

Last week, Monsanto said it received a registration from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency for its YieldGard insect-protected corn. Monsanto said the registration covers technology licensed to Cargill Hybrid Seeds, DeKalb Genetics Corp and Golden Harvest Seeds, as well as Pioneer.

"Although supplies will be limited during this introductory year, we will be offering eight hybrids in a broad range of maturities for spring 1997 planting," Scott Erickson, corn marketing manager for Pioneer in North America, said in a statement.
He added that EPA terms and conditions associated with insect resistance strategies will limit Bt hybrid sales in some cotton growing areas of the United States.
Pioneer said it has initiated several long-term research projects for its Bt products.
